# Port the post-checkout / post-merge / post-rewrite hooks to the repo-root v2 wrappers

**Headline:** The three committed Worklog hooks are `worklog:post-pull-hook:v1`
wrappers that `exec` an absolute per-machine path,
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`. When that path is absent (any
machine where `scripts/install_pi.sh` has not run), every checkout, merge and
`git worktree add` fails with `exec: … not found` (exit 127) and the post-pull
`wl sync` never runs — which broke `wl sync` in this repository on 2026-10-30
until `scripts/install_pi.sh` was re-run.

## Problem statement

`SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` closed the "nothing creates the central script" half of
the problem by installing it from `install_pi.sh`. The remaining half is the
hard-coded absolute path itself: the hooks only work on a machine where the
installer ran, and a relocation or a fresh host silently disables the Worklog
sync. `ContentCreator` already migrated its hooks to `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2`
wrappers that resolve the delegate from the repository root
(`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) and fail open; this repository still ships the
v1 form.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** — `implement.py start/finish` and `wl sync` abort
  with exit 127 whenever git creates a worktree or checks out a branch on a
  machine without the central hook.
- **Developers on a fresh clone or a renamed checkout** — merges error on a
  hook they did not write and cannot see.
- **Producers** — Worklog data silently stops syncing when the hook errors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge` and
      `.githooks/post-rewrite` carry the `worklog:post-pull-hook:v2` marker,
      resolve `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`,
      `cd` there, and `exec` it.
- [ ] All three wrappers are fail-open: no resolvable repository root, a missing
      delegate, or a missing `wl`/`worklog` exits 0 so a merge or checkout never
      fails because of the hook.
- [ ] `WORKLOG_SKIP_POST_PULL=1` still short-circuits the sync (delegate
      behaviour unchanged).
- [ ] Tests prove the hooks work with `$HOME` unset or pointing at a sandbox and
      without any `$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull`, from the
      repository root and from a subdirectory, for all three wrappers.
- [ ] A test scans `.githooks/` and fails if any file regains a hard-coded
      absolute checkout path (the `ContentCreator` equivalent lives in
      `tests/test_worklog_hooks.py`).
- [ ] `scripts/install_pi.sh` no longer warns that the wrappers do not delegate
      to the central path, and either stops installing the central script or
      documents it as legacy.
- [ ] `docs/dev/` hook documentation describes the v2 wrappers and the fail-open
      contract.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the `docs/dev/` hook pages.

## Constraints

- Keep `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` as the single implementation of the
  post-pull sync; the wrappers stay thin.
- Do not change the pre-push hook or its gates.
- Removal of the central-script install from `install_pi.sh` is optional; if it
  stays, it must not be required for the hooks to work.

## Existing state

```
$ cat .githooks/post-checkout
#!/bin/sh
# worklog:post-pull-hook:v1
# Wrapper that delegates to central Worklog post-pull script (committed hooks).
exec "/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull" "$@"
```

Observed failure (2026-10-30, `wl sync` in this repository):

```
✗ Sync failed: Command failed with exit code 127: git worktree add --detach '…/.worklog/tmp-worktree-yZC0Kd/wt' 'refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data'
Preparing worktree (detached HEAD a07575c13)
/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.githooks/post-checkout: 4: exec: /home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull: not found
```

Running `scripts/install_pi.sh` created
`$HOME/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` and the sync then succeeded — a
workaround, not a fix.

## Desired change

Replace the three v1 wrappers with the v2 wrapper (see
`ContentCreator/.githooks/post-merge` for the canonical text), extend
`tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` (or a new hook test module) with the
`$HOME`-independent cases, and update `scripts/install_pi.sh` and the docs to
match.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.githooks/post-checkout` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-merge` — v2 wrapper
- `.githooks/post-rewrite` — v2 wrapper
- `tests/test_install_pi_post_pull_hook.py` — hook behaviour without the central
  script; hard-coded-path scan
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — stop requiring the central script; drop the
  delegation warning
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — v2 wrapper contract (the post-pull hook page;
  there is no `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md`)

## Plan: changelog

- `2026-11-14` (plan skill, SA-0MVVFAM0P002PZYI): pre-check returned
  `skip` (effort Small, risk Low) so no child decomposition was created; the
  item is sized for direct implementation.
- `2026-11-14` (plan skill): corrected the `Key Files` doc reference from
  `docs/dev/pre-push-hook.md` (does not exist) to `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`,
  which is the post-pull hook page that already documents the portable
  wrappers and fail-open contract and must be updated to the v2 shape.
- `2026-11-14` (plan skill): noted that `SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX` already made the
  committed wrappers portable (repo → local → `$HOME` resolution with the
  `v1` marker); the remaining work is the v2 repo-root-only shape (per
  `ContentCreator/.githooks/post-merge`), so the "existing state" described
  above is historical context, not the current checkout.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` works when executed from the
  repository root; that is how `post-merge` already invokes it.
- **Risk (low):** a `post-checkout` run inside `.worklog/tmp-worktree-*` (the
  Worklog data branch) would sync from that temporary checkout. Mitigation: the
  delegate is already fail-open and warns on failure; verify it does not
  recurse when the temporary worktree has no `.worklog`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** consolidating the hooks with the ContentCreator copy
  into one shared installer is tempting. Record that separately; this item only
  ports the v2 wrapper shape.

## Related work

- `SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP` — installs the central post-pull script (the other half
  of the same failure mode).
- `SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX` — fail-open portability warning added to
  `install_pi.sh`.
- `OSL-0MVVE7V84007DQD0` (ContentCreator) — the item whose `wl sync` surfaced
  this failure.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MU8CRX1X008IORP** – Chore: install central wl post-pull hook (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) missing (completed)
- **SA-0MVK1Q30O0067NXX** – Commit hooks exec a missing absolute path (/home/rgardler/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) → git worktree add and wl sync fail (completed)
- **SA-0MVK2PK7F002LET6** – SorraAgents committed git hooks exec a missing central script (~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull) (completed)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: abort, absent, absolute, acceptance, add (+205 more)

# implement.py Key Files gate misses the bold-inside-heading form

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-31). That RISE item was filed during `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` and is deleted once this item exists (producer decision Q1 = re-file here).

**Headline:** The Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate in `implement.py` parses only
`## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)` and a bare `**Key Files:**` line, so a
work item whose section is written `## **Key Files:**` (bold marker nested in an
H2/H3) yields no key files, dirty-file relevance becomes unjudgeable, and
`implement.py start` aborts on a dirty checkout even when every dirty path is
unrelated. Make the heading matcher form-agnostic and lock it down with
regression tests.

## Problem statement

`_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` matches
`#{1,6}\s*Key Files.*` (heading) **or** `\*\*Key Files:?\*\*.*` (bold line) — but
not the combination `## **Key Files:**`, because after the `## ` prefix the next
token is `**`, not `Key Files`. `extract_key_files_from_description()` then
returns `[]`, `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` reports *"no Key Files section in
the work item description — cannot judge dirty-file relevance"*, and
`phase_start` takes the conservative abort-and-ask branch even though the
description does list key files and the dirty paths demonstrably do not overlap
them. The gate's conservative default is correct; it is being tripped by a
parser gap rather than by a real risk.

## Evidence

Reproduced in this session against the installed skill tree
(`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `SorraAgents/skill`):

| form | `extract_key_files_from_description` |
|---|---|
| `## Key Files` | `['a/b.ts', 'tests/c.test.ts']` |
| `## Key Files (predicted)` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `**Key Files:**` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `## **Key Files:**` | `[]` |
| `### **Key Files:**` | `[]` |

- **Corpus prevalence (consumer store):** 9 of 386 items in the
  `tce-the-rising` store use the bold-inside-heading form — the face-off tie
  epic parent RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU and its eight children
  (RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX, RISE-0MVRMI7GR006QH44, RISE-0MVRMI9F0007HXBW,
  RISE-0MVRMIB7Z008P1HB, RISE-0MVRMID1B0098HAY, RISE-0MVRMIF0T008A72W,
  RISE-0MVRMIGXS0073HDX, RISE-0MVRMIISC009TXYX). For comparison: 297 items use
  a plain heading, 52 a bare bold line, 28 none.
- **Observed stall:** `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` aborted on child
  RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX (Key Files: `tests/the-rising/risingMatchHarness.ts`,
  `tests/the-rising/TheRisingRules.test.ts`) although the only dirty paths were
  six untracked `standups/*.md` files — zero overlap, i.e. exactly the
  documented "proceed, leave the dirty files untouched" case. The operator
  worked around it by pre-creating the worktree and running `start` from inside
  it (where the main-checkout gate is skipped by design).
- **No direct test coverage** of `extract_key_files_from_description`,
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files` or `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` exists under
  `skill/implement/tests/`, so this class of gap is invisible to the suite.
- The framework does **not** emit the H2-wrapped form itself:
  `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` (`_parse_key_files_section`,
  `validate_key_files_format`) and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` use a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line, so both families of form must keep working.

## Users

- **Implement-skill agent (primary)**: "When I start an item whose Key Files
  section is written `## **Key Files:**`, I want `start` to read those paths and
  let me proceed when the dirty files are unrelated, so I do not have to
  hand-work around a gate that already has the information it needs."
- **Producer / operator (secondary)**: "When a downtime run dispatches a child
  session, I want `start` to proceed or abort for a real reason, so unattended
  runs do not stall on a parsing bug."
- **Framework maintainer**: "I want every accepted Key Files heading form
  covered by a table-driven test, so a future edit to the extractor cannot
  silently drop a form."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `extract_key_files_from_description()` returns the listed paths for
  any `Key Files` heading regardless of emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or
  case: `## **Key Files:**`, `### **Key Files:**`, `## **Key Files (predicted):**`,
  `#### key files`, asserted by a table-driven unit test in
  `skill/implement/tests/`.
- **AC2** — Every currently supported form keeps working, asserted in the same
  table: `## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)`, `### Key Files`, and a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line; plus the tolerant bare-marker variants —
  `  **Key Files:**` (indented/whitespace) and `**Key Files**` (no colon).
- **AC3** — `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` proceeds (`can_proceed: true`)
  when the description uses `## **Key Files:**` and the dirty paths do not
  overlap those entries, and still aborts (`can_proceed: false`) when a dirty
  path does overlap, or when the description has no Key Files section at all.
- **AC4** — Extraction still stops at the end of the Key Files section: a
  following `#`/`##`/`###` heading or standalone bold section marker terminates
  the list, so prose lines and acceptance-criteria bullets never leak in as
  paths (regression guard for the SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2 defect class).
- **AC5** — A regression test demonstrates the defect before the fix (red on the
  current implementation, green after), and the end-to-end path is verified:
  `implement.py start` on a `## **Key Files:**` item with only unrelated dirty
  paths creates the worktree, leaves the dirty files untouched and records the
  decision in a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — The gate's safety properties are preserved: no
  stash/commit/revert of dirty files, and abort-and-ask still fires for "no Key
  Files section" and for any overlap.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments and docstrings in `implement.py` and the accepted-forms
  list in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree
  gate, SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR) plus the project README and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`** plus its tests and docs
  (producer decision Q2 = A). The two sibling parsers — `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — are fixed by linked follow-up
  items (below), not here.
- **The gate stays conservative.** No Key Files section, or any overlapping
  dirty path, must still abort and ask. Nothing here may turn the gate into a
  whitelist or relax "never stash/commit/revert the user's work".
- **Must not regress existing forms.** The new matcher may be more tolerant but
  never stricter: an item that starts cleanly today must still start cleanly.
- **Minimal surface.** No new configuration knob or environment variable.
- **UK English** in comments, docstrings and docs.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` (~line 1671),
  `extract_key_files_from_description()` (~1676),
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files()` (~1712), `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()`
  (~1742), and the `phase_start` call site (~5993) that turns a
  `can_proceed: false` verdict into the dirty-worktree abort.
- The extractor's loop already terminates on a `#`-heading line or a non-bullet
  line starting with `**`; only the initial heading match is wrong. A new
  matcher must not let the matched heading's own bold marker look like the
  section end.
- `skill/implement/tests/` has suites for the start/finish gates but none that
  exercises the Key Files extractor or the relevance classifier.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate
  section) enumerates the three supported forms and needs the tolerant list.

## Desired change

1. Replace the two-branch heading regex with one form-agnostic matcher: an
   optional H1–H6 prefix, an optional `**` bold marker, `Key Files`, an optional
   parenthetical qualifier and optional closing `**`/`:`, matched
   case-insensitively — while still requiring `Key Files` to be the first
   content token (so `## Notes on Key Files` stays unmatched unless it matches
   today).
2. Keep the section terminator and the bullet/backtick path parsing unchanged
   (including `path → note`).
3. Add the table-driven tests (AC1–AC5) and the end-to-end `start` regression.
4. Update the docstring/comment and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — form-agnostic `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE`,
  extractor terminator/docstrings; classifier branches unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_key_files_extraction.py` — new table-driven tests
  for the accepted forms, the terminator behaviour and
  `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` proceed/abort decisions.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — accepted-forms list in the
  Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate section.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — over/under-matching:** tightening "first content token" could make a
  heading that matches today (e.g. `## Key Files and notes`) stop matching.
  Keep the match at least as wide as today; assert the old forms in the table.
- **Risk — terminator drift:** after accepting the new form the loop must not
  treat the matched heading's own `**` as a section end.
- **Risk — untestable "it works now" claims:** the AC5 end-to-end check needs a
  deliberately dirty main checkout, so it must leave the dirty files untouched
  and clean up after itself (or exercise the classifier/`phase_start` seam
  directly).
- **Assumption:** the H2-wrapped form is agent-authored markdown, not framework
  output — so the fix belongs in the tolerant parser, not in the plan skill's
  emitter.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the plan/audit parsers are separate items (below);
  anything further discovered goes to `discovered-from` items, not this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR** — Allow implement.py start to create a clean worktree
  when main checkout is dirty: introduced the gate and the three-form parser;
  this item fixes its blind spot.
- **SA-0MUYEV5AO006V0HK** — project-local skill extensions / dirty-tree
  exemptions (the other documented relaxation path of the same gate).
- **SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2** — `plan_helpers._parse_key_files_section` did not stop
  at Markdown headings (same failure family: section-boundary parsing).
- **SA-0MTYP6T2I00396J7** — generated `standups/` output not gitignored: the
  source of the six dirty files in the reproduction.
- **SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ** — the previous framework fix discovered from a
  tce-the-rising implement run (disposition precedent for this re-filing).
- **RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU** — Face-off tie epic whose children carry the
  `## **Key Files:**` form and whose drive run hit the abort.

## Linked follow-up items (producer decision Q2 = B and C)

- **Follow-up 1 — plan parser:** `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  `_parse_key_files_section` / `validate_key_files_format` should accept the same
  heading forms so plan validation does not report a missing/empty Key Files
  section for a validly-written description.
- **Follow-up 2 — audit parser:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`'s Key
  Files extraction (`^#{0,4}\s*Key Files.*?$`) has the same blind spot, which
  omits the item's files from the Phase 2 file-scope manifest. Either fix it
  locally or extract one shared, heading-aware Key Files helper consumed by
  implement/plan/audit.

Both are filed with `discovered-from:<this item>`; their SA ids are recorded in
this item's comments.

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

Interview raised on RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (comment `RISE-C0MVWO1N400000N41`),
answered by the producer in-session on 2026-10-31. Answers are transcribed
verbatim.

- **Q1 — Which worklog/store carries the fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A - delete this when filed"** → the fix is re-filed in
  the SorraAgents worklog as this item (with `discovered-from:RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8`)
  and the RISE item is deleted once this item exists. Recommended option A was
  accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q2 — How wide is the parser fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A, with B and C as linked follow-ups"** →
  `implement.py` only in this item; the plan parser (B) and audit parser (C) are
  filed as linked follow-up items rather than folded in. Recommended option A
  was accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q3 — Which heading variants must be accepted?**
  **Answer (producer): "B + C"** → accept any `Key Files` heading regardless of
  emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or case (B), **and** tolerate whitespace /
  colon variants of the bare bold marker (C). Recommended option was B; the
  producer widened it to B+C, reflected in AC1/AC2. Source: interactive reply,
  this session.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — Does the framework emit the
  H2-wrapped form?** No: `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py:127-160` and
  `skill/plan/SKILL.md:181,306` specify a bare `**Key Files:**` line; the
  H2-wrapped form in the consumer store was authored into descriptions directly.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — How many items are affected in the
  consumer store?** 9 of 386 (`tce-the-rising`), all inside the face-off tie
  epic. Evidence: SQL scan of that store's `workitems.description`.

# audit Key Files extraction misses the bold-inside-heading form

**discovered-from:SA-0MVWO79DA006FYCQ** (producer decision Q2 = C: fixed as a linked follow-up, not folded into that item).

## Problem

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` extracts an item's Key Files with the regex `^#{0,4}\s*Key Files.*?$` (line ~7313). A description that writes the section as `## **Key Files:**` (heading with a nested bold marker) does not match, so the item's own files are omitted from the Phase 2 file-scope manifest and from the code-quality scope fallback. Phase 2 then instructs the model to read only the remaining in-scope files, which can produce "outside the manifest" verdicts against the audited item's real changes.

**Impact:** Items written with `## **Key Files:**` are audited with an incomplete file scope, causing false-positive verdicts against the item's actual changes.

**Prevalence:** 9 of 386 items in the `tce-the-rising` store use `## **Key Files:**`.

## Users

- Audit runner — consumes Key Files to build the Phase 2 file-scope manifest.
- Audited work-item author — expects their own changes to be in-scope and not flagged as "outside the manifest".

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Key Files extractor (`_extract_key_files`) returns the listed paths for `## **Key Files:**`, `### **Key Files:**` and the bare `**Key Files:**` form — covered by a table-driven test in `skill/audit/tests/`.
2. The Phase 2 file-scope manifest includes entries parsed from `## **Key Files:**` headings, asserted by a test that builds the manifest from such a description.
3. Code-quality scope resolution no longer degrades to "no scope" for an item whose only Key Files heading is the bold-inside-heading form.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Every currently matched form must continue to work (backward-compatible).
- The section bound must remain correct: a following heading or bold marker still ends the list.
- Prefer sharing code with the implement and plan Key Files extractors rather than introducing a third copy.

## Existing state

- `audit_runner.py` line ~7313: `r"^#{0,4}\s*Key Files.*?$"` — matches H1–H5 only, no bold handling.
- `implement.py` (SA-0MVWO79DA006FYCQ) uses: `r"^\s*(?:#{1,6}\s*Key Files.*|\*\*Key Files:?\*\*.*)\s*$"` — H1–H6 + bare `**Key Files:**`.
- `plan_helpers.py` uses `stripped.startswith("**Key Files:**")` — only handles the bold form.

## Desired change

1. Make the Key Files heading match form-agnostic in the same way as the implement-skill fix (SA-0MVWO79DA006FYCQ): optional H1–H6 prefix, optional bold marker around `Key Files`, optional parenthetical qualifier, optional closing `**`/`:`, case-insensitive; plus whitespace/colon-tolerant bare `**Key Files:**` lines.
2. Prefer extracting one shared, heading-aware Key Files helper consumed by implement, plan and audit (see the plan follow-up SA-0MVWO7J4I004AAQU) over a third copy of the regex — record the choice in the item.
3. Keep every currently matched form working and keep the section bound (a following heading or bold marker still ends the list).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Key Files heading extraction (`_extract_key_files`) and `_resolve_code_quality_scope` / file-scope manifest call sites.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_file_scope.py` — bold-inside-heading manifest coverage.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVWO79DA006FYCQ** — implement.py Key Files gate misses the bold-inside-heading form (sibling fix).
- **SA-0MVWO7J4I004AAQU** — plan Key Files parser misses the bold-inside-heading form (sibling item).
- **SA-0MUJNZ5RN0078B5M**, **SA-0MUI5ZYO6002W3KD** — file-scope/code-quality scope fixes in the same manifest machinery.

## Risks & assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Regex change could match unintended heading variants | Table-driven tests covering all known forms + a negative test for non-matching patterns |
| Shared extractor would require changes to implement and plan | Documented in the plan follow-up item; implement first in audit, defer sharing |
| Section-bound logic (`break` on next heading) may need adjustment for bold markers | Reuse the implement.py section-bound logic as reference |

## Appendix

(No interview questions — the work item was sufficiently defined for intake to proceed without an interview.)

# Release gate (merge-dev-to-main.sh) discards the runner JSON, so a dev→main release cannot say why the suite gate failed

Discovered-from: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (during `/skill:plan`).

## Problem

`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` runs the full-suite release
gate as:

```bash
if python3 "$TEST_RUNNER" --scope full --strict-git-env 2>&1; then
```

The runner's machine-readable result is never requested and the exit code is
the only signal, so a slot-contention expiry (`slot_busy`), a killed suite
(`killed`) and a genuine red suite all produce the same message: "Full test
suite failed on the merged dev→main tree — the release is blocked." The
operator cannot tell "fix the code" from "wait for a slot / raise
`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`", and a release attempt can burn hours of queue wait before
failing indistinguishably from a real regression.

The pre-push hook gets the equivalent fix under **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (its
AC2/AC3); this item is the same defect on the release path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The release gate consumes the runner's machine-readable result and reports the same `gate_reason=<code>` vocabulary the pre-push hook uses.
- [ ] A slot-contention or killed-run failure prints a distinct message with the remediation hint (wait then re-run, or raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`), while a red suite keeps its current message.
- [ ] The gate still fails closed (non-zero exit, no release) in every failure case, and `SHIP_TEST_SKIP=1` still bypasses it.
- [ ] A hermetic test (following `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py`) pins the classification for slot contention, killed and red-suite cases.

## Notes

- Reuse the shared classifier introduced by SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI rather than a second copy; this item is deliberately **not** a child of it so the release path can ship independently.
- UK English throughout.

## Goal

As a producer/agent, I want a single, reproducible per-test-file **keep / rework / prune** verdict that combines churn, mutation, anti-pattern and runtime evidence, so test-value decisions are made from one reconciled report rather than four separate reads.

## Problem statement

Today the evidence for test value is fragmented across `skill/test-churn` (evolution/growth), the mutation-testing campaign (`SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`, fault detection), `evaluate_usefulness.py` + `test-writing-guidelines.md` (static anti-patterns) and the test runner (runtime/flake). Each answers a different question; none produces an auditable per-file verdict. Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` needs a repeatable classify → prove → report pipeline, and this skill is the missing connective tissue between those signals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ingests, per test file: churn metrics (rewrite/growth/stability), mutation score, anti-pattern verdicts, and runtime/flake data when available.
- [ ] Emits one verdict per file — `keep`, `rework` or `prune` — with the evidence for that verdict recorded.
- [ ] Totals reconcile: verdict counts sum to files in scope, and every verdict cites at least one evidence source.
- [ ] Produces `test_value_report.md` + `test_value_data.json` with documented definitions and limitations.
- [ ] Orchestrates the existing analysers; it does not reimplement churn, mutation or anti-pattern detection.
- [ ] Missing inputs degrade honestly (the report states which signals were absent; it never fabricates a verdict).
- [ ] Reproducible (pinned inputs, documented command, deterministic ordering) and covered by tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the analysed project.
- Must not turn a heuristic into an automatic deletion; `prune` is advisory and conservative.
- No per-project hardcoded paths; project root is an argument.
- Follows the repository skill contract and `$(skill_path ...)` shared-library resolution.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (classify/prove/report).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (behavioural evidence arm).

## Goal

As a test-value reviewer, I want a cheap static measure of how a test asserts and how much it relies on mocks, so I can pre-filter the suites that mutation testing should examine and give `toHaveBeenCalledWith`-style coupling an enforceable signal.

## Problem statement

`evaluate_usefulness.py` detects only crude anti-patterns (source-grep, placeholder, zero assertions, self-referential). It cannot distinguish a test that asserts observable behaviour from one that asserts internal collaborator calls, nor quantify mock density — yet mock density is a central independent variable in the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults. Without this signal, the mutation campaign has no cheap way to choose where to spend its runtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parses TypeScript/JavaScript (and ideally Python) test files and reports per file: assertion count, assertions on internal collaborators vs public behaviour, mock/stub/spy count and ratio, and tests with no meaningful assertion.
- [ ] Flags `toHaveBeenCalledWith`/mock-call assertions on internal collaborators as a distinct, actionable signal (aligned with `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G`).
- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with documented definitions and conservative thresholds.
- [ ] Handles dynamic/indirect assertion styles without crashing, and reports uncertainty rather than a false verdict.
- [ ] Runs as a cheap pre-filter (no test execution) and documents that it is a proxy, not ground truth.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Static analysis only; never executes the target project's tests.
- Conservative: uncertainty is reported, never auto-pruned.
- Language-neutral entry point with per-language adapters; no hardcoded project paths.

## Related work

- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.
- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing (ground truth).

## Goal

As a maintainer of a large test suite, I want to detect near-duplicate test blocks and files, so additive accumulation can be measured and redundant coverage pruned with evidence.

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measured large net test growth (+137,022 lines on the reference project) with a low rewrite ratio — the failure mode is additive accumulation, not churn. `evaluate_usefulness.py`'s "duplicate coverage" check is a heuristic and cannot find near-duplicates introduced through different import paths or copy-paste variation. Without clone detection, redundancy grows unnoticed because nothing forces a re-examination.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Detects near-duplicate test blocks (within and across files) using normalised AST/token similarity, not raw text matching.
- [ ] Reports clusters with file, line range and similarity score, ordered by redundancy.
- [ ] Distinguishes legitimate repetition (table-driven cases, parameterised variants) from redundant duplication, and defaults to reporting rather than removal.
- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with thresholds and limitations documented.
- [ ] Performance is bounded on a large suite (documented sampling/scope options).
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Read-only; no automatic deletion.
- Conservative thresholds; a false "duplicate" verdict is worse than a miss.
- No hardcoded project paths.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (additive accumulation is its stated failure mode).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing; this analyser is a complementary cheap signal.
- `skill/test-churn`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`.

discovered-from:SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O

## Notes

Created from the intake discussion on `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`. Lower urgency than the mutation and assertion-quality arms, but it directly attacks the accumulation problem the epic describes.
data.title: Add near-duplicate test detection to find redundant test coverage

## Goal

As a producer, I want per-test runtime and flake history so I can express test value as fault detection per second of suite runtime and bound the cost of periodic mutation campaigns.

## Problem statement

Test value is currently measured without its cost. The test runner reports suite-level timing, but there is no per-test timing or flake history, so a valuable-but-slow test and a worthless-but-slow test are indistinguishable, and mutation-campaign runtime cannot be allocated sensibly. The test-value epic (`SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`, AC7) also needs before/after runtime evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test runner records per-test duration and a bounded flake history across runs.
- [ ] Emits a machine-readable report consumable by the test-value aggregator (churn/mutation/runtime join).
- [ ] Overhead is bounded and documented; normal runs stay within the existing runtime budget.
- [ ] Flake detection is deterministic for repeated failures and does not hide genuine failures.
- [ ] Integrated into the existing `skill/test` runner rather than a new measurement skill.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Must not change the pass/fail semantics of the test runner.
- History storage is bounded (retention policy documented).
- Follows the test-execution policy: agents still invoke tests only via the test skill; infrastructure gates are out of scope.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (AC7 runtime).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing (runtime bound).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`.

Created from the intake discussion on `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`. This is a `skill/test` enhancement, not a new standalone measurement skill.

# Intake Brief: Repeat producer actions in red on the final report conclusion

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report`) lists blocking producer
actions in `## Producer Actions`, but the `## Conclusion` — the last thing the
operator reads — does not repeat them. When a session ends with something the
producer must do (answer a question, make a decision, grant an approval), the
operator can miss it in the body of a long report. Repeating any genuine
producer action in the Conclusion in red makes the blocking call-to-action
impossible to overlook.

## Users

- **Producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports in the pi TUI: wants the
  blocking action to stand out at the end of the report, not be buried mid-page.
- **Agent (intake/plan/implement/audit/…) authoring the report**: keeps passing
  blocking actions via `--producer-actions`; the renderer handles the red
  repetition deterministically (no per-skill change).

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a skill session needs a decision from me, I want that
  decision repeated in red in the conclusion so I cannot miss it."
- "As a producer, when nothing is required of me, I do not want a red warning in
  the conclusion."
- "As an agent, I want the renderer to do this automatically so every skill
  behaves the same way."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the normalised producer actions are a genuine, non-`None needed`
   action, `render_report()` appends the action text **verbatim** to the
   `## Conclusion` section, wrapped in ANSI SGR red (`\x1b[31m…\x1b[0m`) with a
   `⚠️ Producer action required:` lead-in. Verified by unit test asserting the
   escape sequences and the exact action text inside `## Conclusion`.
2. When no producer actions are supplied, or the supplied text is routine
   workflow progression that normalises to `None needed`, the Conclusion
   contains no ANSI escape sequences and no repeated action text. Verified by
   unit tests (absent actions; `Proceed to /skill:plan`; `Review the brief, then
   run /skill:plan`).
3. Colour can be disabled with a new `--no-colour` CLI flag **or** the standard
   `NO_COLOR` environment variable (non-empty). In that mode the Conclusion
   still repeats the action in plain text with the `⚠️` marker and contains no
   ANSI escape sequences. Verified by unit tests for both opt-outs.
4. Multi-line / multi-action producer text is repeated verbatim (line breaks
   preserved) and the rest of the report is unchanged: section order,
   `## Producer Actions` → `## Notes` → `## Conclusion`, the existing
   completed/incomplete conclusion sentences, and the `</end_session>`
   terminator. Verified by regression tests.
5. `skill/report/SKILL.md` documents the conditional red repetition in the
   canonical template, the layout rules, and the colour opt-out
   (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`) alongside the existing icon opt-out. Verified
   by document review.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Implement in the shared renderer only (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  plus a small shared colour helper — do not fork report logic into the ~17
  calling skills.
- Repeat **after** routine-next-step normalisation (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW): a
  routine next step must never produce red text.
- Do not use TTY detection to decide colour: the CLI's stdout is captured/piped
  by agents before being pasted into the final response, so TTY detection would
  disable the feature exactly where it is needed. Opt-out must be explicit
  (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`).
- Colour is decorative: the `⚠️` marker and the plain action text must carry the
  meaning when colour is unavailable, so the report stays readable in
  non-ANSI consumers (GitHub, plain-text logs).
- No new runtime dependency; pure-Python, offline-testable.
- Do not change `## Producer Actions` semantics, the pane-status derivation, or
  the existing conclusion wording.

## Existing state

- `render_report()` renders `## Producer Actions` from the normalised
  `producer_actions` string (`None needed` when absent), then `## Notes`, then
  `## Conclusion`.
- The Conclusion currently emits one of two fixed sentences based on AC
  verdicts (`_derive_session_status`): completed → "This completes … Ready for
  `<next_action>`."; incomplete → "… is incomplete. Requires attention
  (`<next_action>`)." Nothing else is appended.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` already provides `icons_enabled(no_icons, env)`
  honouring `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` — the convention to mirror for
  colour, but colour must be a separate switch (`WL_NO_ICONS` must not disable
  colour).
- No ANSI/colour handling exists anywhere in the report renderer today (the
  only ANSI in the repo is in `tests/integration/test-worktree-workflow.sh`).

## Desired change

- Add `colour_enabled(no_colour=False, env=None)` (and `RED`/`RESET` constants)
  to `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`: enabled by default; disabled by
  `--no-colour` or a non-empty `NO_COLOR`.
- In `render_report()`, after the existing conclusion sentence(s), when the
  normalised producer actions are not `None needed`, append a blank line and a
  red line: `⚠️ Producer action required: <verbatim action text>`. Apply
  `RED … RESET` only when colour is enabled.
- Thread an optional `no_colour: bool = False` parameter through
  `render_report()`, `render_report_from_workitem()`, `render_from_wl()` and the
  CLI, adding the `--no-colour` flag.
- Update `skill/report/SKILL.md` (template, layout rules, example, colour
  opt-out) and the `README.md` report-helper bullet to mention the red
  repetition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — conditional red repetition in the
  Conclusion; `no_colour` plumbing and `--no-colour` flag.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` helper + `RED`/`RESET`
  constants mirroring `icons_enabled()`.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — new tests: red repetition,
  no-repetition for absent/routine actions, `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR` fallback,
  multi-line preservation, structure regression.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` unit tests.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — template/layout/example + colour opt-out docs.
- `README.md` — report-helper bullet: note the red repetition of blocking
  producer actions in the Conclusion.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** — "Don't include producer actions that are next steps"
  (completed): established normalisation to `None needed`; the red repetition
  must run after it.
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — "Misleading completion message on LLM summaries"
  (completed): made the Conclusion reflect session status; this item extends the
  same section.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — "Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion" (completed): established the ✅/⚠️/🚫 status colour semantics this
  feature reuses for a red call-to-action.
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill" (completed): origin of the canonical report contract.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "red font" means ANSI SGR red in terminal output.** The report
  is rendered to stdout and pasted into the pi TUI; ANSI is the only mechanism
  that reliably colours that path. If the producer expects Markdown/HTML
  colouring, the brief should be revised before implementation (documented in
  the Appendix).
- **Assumption — red repeats blocking actions only.** Because routine workflow
  progression is normalised to `None needed` first, it can never trigger red;
  this avoids the false "producer is blocking" signal fixed by
  SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW.
- **Assumption — no TTY detection.** Explicit opt-out only, because agent-captured
  stdout is not a TTY.
- **Risk — ANSI leakage into non-terminal consumers** (GitHub, PRs, plain logs).
  Mitigation: `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR`, plus the `⚠️` marker and plain text so the
  meaning survives even if escapes are stripped or shown literally.
- **Risk — colour-blindness / theme contrast.** Mitigation: the `⚠️` marker and
  the words "Producer action required" carry the signal; colour is decorative.
- **Risk — multi-line producer text.** Mitigation: wrap the whole block once and
  test line-break preservation rather than prefixing each line.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent ideas (colouring the `## Producer Actions` section,
  colourising AC verdicts, HTML-export colour) are out of scope — record as
  separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'red font' mean for a Markdown report rendered by the LLM/TUI —
  ANSI escape codes, HTML `<span style=\"color:red\">`, or plain emphasis?"
  — **Answer (repo research + design analysis):** ANSI SGR red. The report is
  printed to stdout and pasted into the terminal-rendered TUI; raw ANSI passes
  through and colours the terminal, whereas inline HTML styles are not honoured
  by the Markdown→terminal path and GitHub strips `style` attributes. Recorded
  as an assumption; the producer can request an HTML/bold variant at review.
  No interactive round was required for the rest of the brief.
- Q: "Should routine next-step actions (e.g. 'Proceed to /skill:plan') also be
  repeated in red?" — **Answer (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW contract):** No. Routine
  workflow progression is normalised to `None needed` and must never be shown as
  a blocking red action; only genuine, current-stage actions are repeated.
- Q: "Should colour be auto-detected (TTY) or explicitly opt-out?" — **Answer
  (design analysis):** Explicit opt-out only. Agent-captured stdout is not a
  TTY, so TTY detection would silently disable the feature on the exact path
  that needs it. `--no-colour` and `NO_COLOR` are the opt-outs.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVQ1QM9L0083KAW** – Producer Actions contract: docs and skill templates (completed)
- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** – Don't include producer actions that are next steps (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: action, actions, conclusion, final, llm, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: action, actions, final, llm, output, producer, red, repeat, them, there
data.title: Repeat producer actions in red font on final LLM action report

## Goal

`_git_commit_evidence` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` resolves a
stranded child's pushed-commit evidence with
`git log <ref> --grep <child_id> -n 1`. `--grep` matches the **whole commit
message including the body**, so a commit that merely *mentions* a work-item id
counts as that item's work.

Observed 2026-11-01 during the epic drive for SA-0MVX1M6HH004YPX2: driven child
SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 timed out after 3600 s with its own commit (`9119e4117`)
still unpushed in its worktree, and `drive` reported it as *stranded* with
evidence `0fb0e4305` — the **sibling** child's (SA-0MVX31GLC002IPR8) commit,
whose body names SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 as the future home of the detection
module. The verdict told the operator to `--finalise-stranded` a child whose
work had never been pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Commit evidence matches only commits whose **subject** references the
   work-item id, never a body-only mention.
2. A regression test pins the false-positive: a commit whose body mentions
   another item's id is not evidence for that item.
3. A driven child whose commit is still only in its own worktree is reported
   as non-terminal-with-work, not as stranded on the parent branch.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_git_commit_evidence`
- `skill/implement/tests/` — regression test

# Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in SorraAgents

## Why

This project's worklog database is behind the installed `wl` version. Every `wl` invocation prints:

```
Worklog: database at /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=8 but the application expects schemaVersion=9. Required columns were repaired automatically. see 'wl doctor upgrade' to list and apply pending migrations
```

Required columns are being patched on every invocation instead of migrated, and the git hooks are stale. Discovered during the 2026-11-04 downtime-dispatcher RCA (the same finding exists across the other worklog roots).

## Pending work (from `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`)

### Schema migrations (0)

_None — only hooks below are pending._

### Outdated git hooks

- pre-push, post-checkout, post-merge, post-rewrite, worklog-post-pull

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want this project's worklog schema and git hooks fully up to date, so that `wl` stops auto-patching columns on every call and so every worklog hook behaves like the current template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` afterwards reports `pending: []` and no hook whose `status` is not `up-to-date`.
2. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` was executed against this project's database and applied the migrations listed above.
3. A plain `wl list --json` invocation no longer prints the `schemaVersion=8 … expects schemaVersion=9` warning.
4. **Data-safety check.** The count of items with `needsProducerReview == true` is identical before and after:
   `wl list --json | jq '[.workItems[] | select(.needsProducerReview == true)] | length'`
   Record both numbers on this item.
5. `wl doctor` reports no new findings attributable to this upgrade (any residual finding is recorded on a follow-up item, not ignored).
6. The before/after `--dry-run --json` output is recorded in a comment on this item.

## Plan

1. Capture the baseline: `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` plus the `needsProducerReview` count → comment on this item.
2. Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`.
3. Re-run `--dry-run` (expect nothing pending) and re-check the `needsProducerReview` count (must be unchanged).
4. If the upgrade touched tracked files (`.githooks/`, hook templates), commit them following build → test → commit order.

## Risks & notes

- `--confirm` applies migrations **non-interactively, including UNSAFE ones**. Review the `[UNSAFE]` entries above before running. The database is the runtime source of truth (SQLite); never edit `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and never run `wl import` (destructive).
- If the `needsProducerReview` count changes, STOP, restore, and raise a `bug` against ContextHub's `wl` migration set instead of continuing — the drop/re-add cycle is the suspected cause of the permanent schema-8 oscillation.

## Provenance

Created from the 2026-11-04 overnight zero-dispatch RCA. Pi session `herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004`, log `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-ContextHub--/2026-11-04T07-55-10-163Z_herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004.jsonl`.
data.title: Run wl doctor upgrade --confirm: apply pending schema migrations and refresh outdated git hooks

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:_resolve_merge_base()` returns the **candidate ref name** (`origin/dev`) rather than the SHA resolved by `git merge-base`, and `compute_changed_files()` then runs `git diff --name-only <ref>` against that name.

When an implement worktree's branch base is *behind* the ref (a stale base — e.g. the branch was forked while local `dev` lagged `origin/dev`), diffing against the ref includes **dev-side** commits that are not part of the change set. `select_group_from_changed_files()` then picks test groups for unrelated work.

Discovered-from: WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ (ContextHub store) — the stale-base session in which this was observed.

## Evidence

- Observed on 2026-11-05 in a ContextHub implement session (WL-0MW3JIYIR002RCP8): a docs + `tests/setup-tests.ts` change set ran `npm test -- packages/herdr/src` because the stale base made the diff include dev-side `packages/herdr` commits.
- Current code (`run_tests.py`, `_resolve_merge_base`, ~line 506): the loop runs `git merge-base <candidate> HEAD`, then `return candidate` (the ref name) — the resolved `proc.stdout.strip()` SHA is discarded.
- `compute_changed_files()` (~line 462) passes the returned value straight into `git diff --name-only <base>`.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `implement.py finish` / `run_tests.py --scope changed` — depend on correct changed-file selection.
- **Operators / CI** — depend on changed-scope runs exercising the code that actually changed.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, when my worktree forked from a base behind `origin/dev`, I want changed-scope selection to measure only *my* diff, so the gate runs the right tests.
- As an operator, I want a stale base to degrade into a smaller diff, never into an unrelated named group.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_resolve_merge_base()` returns the SHA resolved by `git merge-base` (falling back to the next candidate only when `merge-base` yields nothing), never a bare ref name.
- [ ] `compute_changed_files()` diffs against a merge-base SHA, so commits that exist on the ref but not on the branch base are excluded from the change set.
- [ ] Regression test: a fixture repo whose branch base is one commit behind the target ref — the changed-file set must contain only the branch's own files, not the ref-side files.
- [ ] Fallback behaviour preserved: with no usable base the function still returns `None` and callers fall back to full scope (no crash).
- [ ] Documentation updated where the changed-scope base semantics are described (`skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`) if the returned value's contract changes.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Probe/read-only of git state; no new runtime dependencies; reuse existing helpers (`_git_inspection_env`, `run_cmd`).
- Behaviour change must be conservative: an unresolved base must still fall back to full scope rather than an empty diff.
- Related but distinct from SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66 (unqualified `origin/dev` ref *ambiguity* with a shadowing local branch) — both live in the same function, so either item may be implemented first; if both are taken together, keep the two fixes as separate commits.
- All written output in UK English.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_resolve_merge_base()` must return the merge-base SHA; `compute_changed_files()` consumes it unchanged.
- `skill/test/tests/` (or the existing test-skill test location) — regression test for a stale-base fixture.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — document the returned-value contract if it is described there.

## Related work

- ContextHub `WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ` — Main-checkout local dev diverged from origin/dev (the stale-base incident; records this hand-off).
- `SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66` — Stale local branch named origin/dev makes origin/dev ambiguous (adjacent defect in the same function).
data.title: run_tests.py _resolve_merge_base returns the ref name instead of the merge-base SHA — changed scope picks up ref-side commits

Discovered while implementing SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE children 1-2 (2026-11-05).

The repository's finish gate and dev-push full-suite runs repeatedly hit the 2700 s per-command timeout under nominal multi-agent host load (full suite observed taking 15-45+ min depending on concurrent suites; verified green runs exist in .worklog/cache). The gate diagnostics classify these as reason=timeout - infrastructure, not code failures - and the documented remedy is to raise timeoutPerCommand in .pi/test-config.json with headroom over a green run's elapsed time.

ACs:
- .pi/test-config.json sets a timeoutPerCommand with headroom over the slowest observed green full-suite run under load (e.g. 5400 s), with the change committed and pushed via a work item.
- A re-run of a previously-timed-out gate for an unchanged tree completes green.

Not urgent (gates converge via cache retry), out of scope for the tracking epic.
data.title: Raise timeoutPerCommand in .pi/test-config.json (full suite exceeds 2700s under multi-agent load)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-14 ~12:06 UTC: Plan skill run (downtime-dispatched, no interactive approver).
- Pre-check: `decision: "plan"` — epic with 17 existing children.
- 17 children already covered the scope (single lint-finding fixes); no new features created,
  no decomposition needed. Added `## Acceptance Criteria` to every child and advanced each to
  `plan_complete` (previously `intake_complete`, no ACs).
- Coverage review: `proceed` (no parent ACs to cover; no conflicts; no children created).
- Effort/Risk: Small / Medium — PERT expected 8.64 h (recommended 13.64 h), via effort-and-risk skill.

discovered-from: SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV

## Goal

As an agent auditing a work item at a freshly pushed `dev` HEAD, I want the audit's full-suite evidence check to reuse the tree-keyed verdict the dev-push gate just recorded for that same commit, so the first audit after every push does not pay for a second identical full-suite run.

## Problem statement

`SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG` (shipped `39ea226b4`) re-keyed the dev-push pre-push gate to the pushed commit's **tree** (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`, `git rev-parse <sha>^{tree}`). The gate therefore no longer writes a loose-worktree-keyed entry for the pushed commit.

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_full_suite_cache_status` still queries the cache worktree-only (`query_cached(command, cwd=..., ttl=AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)`), following the documented contract in `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.3 ("callers that pass nothing keep the historical worktree keys byte for byte (test-skill CLI, audit)").

Consequence, observed live during this epic's own audit at HEAD `ea89bb4e2`:

```
Automatic full-suite verification unavailable: 4 of 4 suite command(s) not verifiably green at HEAD ea89bb4e2 …
```

The gate had already gated that exact commit, yet the audit could not see the verdict and re-executed the whole suite (4 commands, several minutes). Before the tree keying, the gate's worktree-keyed run was mirrored into the main checkout cache and served the audit. This is the mirror image of the reuse gap `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` closed for finish → pre-push, now on the audit path.

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` already solved the identical problem for its own post-push verification (`SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN`, `54d5b79f1`): resolve the pushed commit's tree, query `fingerprint_kind="tree"` first, then fall back to the loose worktree key. The audit path needs the same treatment.

## Desired change

- `_full_suite_cache_status` (and any sibling read-only evidence query that mirrors it, e.g. the `_phase_...` full-suite checks at `audit_runner.py:3559` and `:3767`) resolves the audited HEAD's tree (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`) and queries the tree-kind entry **first**, falling back to the historical worktree query so legacy entries still count.
- A tree-kind entry accepted as evidence is reported with its `fingerprint_kind` and age, so a reused verdict is visible in the audit output rather than implied.
- `query_cached()`'s worktree-only default is unchanged for every other caller (the finish gate's staged-tree semantics depend on it).

## Acceptance criteria

1. An audit at a HEAD whose only cached full-suite evidence is tree-kind (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`, keyed on `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`) reports full-suite evidence **without executing** the suite.
2. A worktree-kind (legacy) entry at the audited HEAD is still accepted, byte-for-byte keying unchanged.
3. An entry recorded for a *different* tree is a miss (a green verdict for another tree is never accepted).
4. The reused verdict's `fingerprint_kind` and age are reported in the audit output/JSON.
5. Deterministic tests cover: tree-kind hit (no execution), legacy worktree hit, different-tree miss, and the unchanged `query_cached()` default for other callers.
6. Documentation is updated: `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.3/§0.4 and the audit-side note in `docs/dev/` describing the audit's evidence query, corrected from "worktree only" to "tree-kind first, worktree fallback".
7. Every new behaviour is exercised by an automated test executed through the test skill, and the full suite passes.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_full_suite_cache_status` and the sibling read-only cache queries.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `query_cached(fingerprint=…, fingerprint_kind=…)` (already supports the tree kind; no new API expected).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — the `_resolve_post_push_verification` precedent (`SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN`) to mirror.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — §0.3/§0.4 contract correction.
- `tests/` — new audit-evidence reuse tests (`tests/test_audit_full_suite_cache_tree.py` or the existing audit home).

## Impact

An agent auditing work at a freshly pushed `dev` HEAD reuses the gate's tree-keyed green verdict instead of re-running the same full suite, cutting the first audit after each push by roughly one full-suite execution.
data.title: Audit: reuse the tree-keyed dev-push gate verdict for full-suite evidence

### Goal
Pure, unit-testable, no-side-effects helper for detecting work-item filing location issues.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. The check deterministically classifies the item as one of ok, foreign, unregistered, absent, or suspicious. Each non-ok classification names the likely correct project (from the sibling scan) and a suggested target prefix.
2. The check lives in a new shared helper skill/shared/filing_location.py (pure, unit-testable, no side effects) invoked from the intake lifecycle script. No other skill changes behaviour in this change.
3. check_filing(item_id, *, cwd, sibling_scan_root, runner) returns FilingCheck with severity ok, foreign, unregistered, absent, or suspicious.
4. Uses existing resolve_worklog_dir, _extract_work_item_prefix, run_wl from status_lifecycle.py (no changes to those modules).
5. Sibling scan is memoized and respects SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT.
6. Content cross-check scans sibling repos' file trees respecting gitignore.
7. No network dependency - only reads config.yaml and runs wl show.
8. Injectable runner for testing.
9. Non-blocking and non-destructive by default - detection never fails intake nor mutates foreign stores; recreation requires explicit flag.
10. Idempotent - re-running the check on the same item yields the same result and never duplicates comments or recreations.

### Key Files
- skill/shared/filing_location.py (new)
- skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py - reuse resolve_worklog_dir, _extract_work_item_prefix, run_wl

# Hermetic interrupted-push verdict tests

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Test-first tracer bullet: write the regression tests **before** the fix. Expectations that
target the new behaviour carry `xfail(strict=True)` until the implementation child removes
the marker; expectations that already hold (the conservative failure paths, the
ancestry-not-equality rule) pass before and after, so a failing test can only be failing on
the behaviour under test.

## Goal

As an implementation agent, I want hermetic, deterministic tests that pin the remote-observed
push verdict, so a later change to `finish`'s push-outcome handling can never silently regress
into reporting a landed push as a failure — nor into claiming success for a commit that never
reached `origin/dev`.

## Context

`finish` treats the exit status of `git push` as the sole verdict on whether the commit reached
`origin/dev`, so a push interrupted after the remote accepted the ref (timeout, process-group
kill, late non-zero exit) is reported as a failure and the item is reset to `open`. The only
remote check today is the post-*success* ancestry assertion
(`_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()`, `implement.py` L8084), which runs after a push already
claimed success — nothing distinguishes "landed but interrupted" from "never landed". No
existing test simulates the race: `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py`,
`tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` and
`skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` all assume the push verdict is truthful.

## Scope

Tests only — no production-code change in this slice. Deliver the failing baselines that the
implementation child turns green, plus the companion tests that prove the preconditions (a
real hermetic push, a reachable bare remote, a real terminal read-back) rather than assuming
them.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — new hermetic suite: probe variants, the three outcomes, sibling-push ancestry.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — existing interrupted-push coverage; extend where a case belongs there.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push baseline (a retry that lands but is reported as failed).
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — reusable `init_bare_remote` / `init_repo` / `add_worktree` / `commit_all` factories; reuse rather than hand-rolling fixtures.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the `FakeGitBoundary` stubbed-boundary harness style for end-to-end `phase_finish` tests.

## Constraints

- **Hermetic:** self-contained bare remote plus clone/worktree under `tmp_path`; never mutate the live checkout's refs, never touch the shared `refs/heads/dev`, no network access.
- **Unambiguous baselines:** pair each new-behaviour `xfail(strict=True)` with a companion that passes before and after, so the preconditions are proven separately instead of being smuggled into the baseline.
- **No hiding failures:** `xfail(strict=True)` only where the expectation targets the not-yet-implemented behaviour.
- **Test execution policy:** no agent-initiated `pytest`/`run_tests.py` invocation outside `/skill:test` (`implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate and the dev-push gate are infrastructure and out of scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Interrupted push variants are covered by unit tests.** Unit tests drive each interrupted-push variant — `PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, and a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward — and assert the remote verification probe runs before any push failure is reported: it verifies whether the commit being pushed is reachable from the remote `dev` tip (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev` plus a fetch of that ref and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>`), is time-bounded, uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite), and applies to the non-fast-forward retry push as well as the first push.
- **Verified-landed success end-to-end.** An end-to-end hermetic test against a bare remote plus a clone under `tmp_path` — where the remote already contains the commit and the push hangs past a short timeout — asserts `report["success"] is True`, the push step is marked `verified_after_failure`, the completion comment naming the commit is posted, the existing success-path cleanup runs (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), and the work item is `completed`/`in_review` with the terminal read-back still passing.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome are distinguished.** Negative tests — a remote without the commit, and a verification probe that itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error) — assert `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Hermetic regression coverage, ancestry not equality.** The new tests are hermetic (self-contained bare remote plus clone under `tmp_path`; no live checkout or live `refs/heads/dev` mutation, no network access) and cover an interrupted push that landed, an interrupted push that did not land, a verification probe failure, and a sibling push advancing `origin/dev` after ours (ancestry, not equality, must be accepted); they fail without the fix (or exercise the new helper directly) and pass with it, reusing the `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` factories.

Add the failing-first regression tests for the stale-branch half of
SA-0MUWNCXHN007K00G (AC3/AC4) so the implementation children have a pinned

- When the target child branch (`wl-<id>-<slug>`) already exists, `phase_start` no longer fails generically: it either reuses the existing worktree/branch (when that branch is at, or fast-forwardable from, the parent branch) or fails with an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command — pinned here by a regression test.

# Recover guarded-child delegation guard

## Goal

Restore the `do-not-delegate` guard in `implement.py` automatic parent
recursion. A complete implementation, test suite and docs edit already exist
in the recoverable commit `91c9b44d1` (from the now-deleted subset item
SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876); this child replays that work onto the current tree
rather than re-deriving it.

Provenance: `git show 91c9b44d1` — files
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md`,
`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`,
`skill/implement/tests/test_phase_parent_do_not_delegate.py` (612 lines).
Its base `c818324b1` is an ancestor of `dev`, so it replays cleanly except
for one deliberate adaptation (below).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `implement.py parent` treats a child tagged `do-not-delegate` as not startable: `_classify_child` returns a dedicated guarded classification (`skip-do-not-delegate`), and both `_next_child_to_implement` and the `phase_parent` child loop skip it, reporting it in the parent report with a distinct action (`"skipped-do-not-delegate"`) and no dependency-`blocked` masking.
- Guarded children are never started, claimed, or re-attempted by `parent`; startable siblings still proceed, and a guarded child is never advanced past (guarded is not terminal, so the parent does not complete while guarded children remain).
- Direct `implement.py start <child>` / `drive <child>` on a `do-not-delegate` child continues to work (that explicit invocation is the documented override); only automatic parent recursion is gated.
- `phase_drive` spawns no session for a guarded child and forwards `guarded_children` for parity with `phase_parent`.
- Guard precedence is adapted to the current tree: `skip-terminal` → `skipped-held` → `skip-in-progress` → `skip-do-not-delegate` → `skip-blocked` → `implement`, so a `blocked` child is never masked as guarded (nor guarded as `blocked`).
- Regression tests cover `_classify_child` / `_next_child_to_implement` with `do-not-delegate` children (guarded skipped, siblings still selected, override path unaffected).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_parent_do_not_delegate.py` is present and passing against the current tree, and the existing parent-recursion/dependency test suites still pass.

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- Replay the guarded-child hunks of `91c9b44d1`: `DO_NOT_DELEGATE_TAG`,
  `ACTION_SKIP_DO_NOT_DELEGATE`, `ACTION_SKIPPED_DO_NOT_DELEGATE`,

- Port the `_next_child_to_implement` skip and the `phase_parent` child-loop

  report field, guarded-specific waiting message) and the `phase_drive`
  forwarding.
- Restore the recovered tests, then add one test pinning the new precedence
  (a guarded child that is also `status: blocked` classifies as guarded).
- Restore the recovered `SKILL.md` / reference-doc guard paragraphs; the docs
  child later owns the stale-branch documentation.

## Constraints

- Replay, do not blind-cherry-pick: `git show 91c9b44d1 -- <path>` is the
  source of truth; resolve the intervening changes by hand and keep the
  current file's style and docstrings.
- No behaviour change for terminal, held, in-progress, blocked or plain
  startable children.
- Idempotent: re-running `parent` on a guarded child performs no claim, no

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_has_do_not_delegate_tag`, `_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `phase_parent`, `phase_drive`

# Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast). When the lock is held, the
agent must re-enter the queue itself, so the skill guidance teaches a hand-rolled
`for attempt in 1..8; implement.py finish ... ; wait_for_job.py --pid <holder> ...`
loop. In the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis this pattern produced the single worst tool
call — **45 minutes** absorbing five consecutive lock holders — and accounted for a
large share of the 37% `wait_for_job` time plus 48 min (7%) of separate `sleep`/`grep`
polling loops. Each fail-fast refusal is also a wasted model round-trip.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch: wants predictable, minimal waiting per session.
- **Implement-skill session** that currently has to script retry loops around
  `implement.py finish`.

User stories:

- As an implement-skill session, I want one `finish` call to wait internally on the
  lock (bounded, with progress) so I do not burn model round-trips on retry loops.
- As an operator watching a batch, I want a waiting session to report who holds the
  lock and to fail with an actionable message only when the bound expires.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a waiting `finish` to perform **one** bounded internal wait on
the flock (with progress), instead of the agent scripting fail-fast retry loops around
it, so concurrent finishes do not multiply round-trips and confusing logs.

## Approach

- Make a positive bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` the guidance default (or
  document setting it) so `finish` waits internally on the flock up to a generous
  bound, emitting progress.
- Remove the `for attempt in ... ; implement.py finish ... ; wait_for_job` retry-loop
  guidance from the implement skill; replace with the single bounded-wait instruction.
- Ensure the internal wait reports the holder and honours `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` cleanly.

## Acceptance criteria

- `implement.py finish` with a positive `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` waits on the
  lock internally within the bound, reporting the holder, and fails with an
  actionable message only when the bound expires.
- The implement skill docs contain no bespoke finish retry-loop pattern; they instruct
  a single bounded wait.
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A test covers: lock held → `finish` waits → holder releases → `finish` proceeds
  (no fail-fast refusal).
- Regression test that the wait is bounded (never hangs) and is signal-safe.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The wait must stay bounded: a configured timeout always terminates the wait with an
  actionable refusal naming the holder and the lock path.
- `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` must release the held lock and the child lock and exit cleanly
  (no orphaned locks).
- Default behaviour must stay safe for unattended sessions: a positive bound must not
  be able to wedge a batch indefinitely.
- Out of scope: changing the single-owner lock semantics or removing the lock.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT = 0.0` (fail fast), env `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`,
  read by `_finish_lock_timeout()`; the bounded wait lives in
  `shared.repo_lock.RepoLock` via `acquire_main_checkout_lock`.
- The implement skill documents the current fail-fast behaviour, and sessions work
  around it with `for attempt ... ; wait_for_job.py --pid <holder>` loops.
- Lock holders are recorded with pid/host metadata, so the holder can already be named
  in a refusal.

## Desired change

`finish` performs one bounded internal wait with progress and holder reporting; the
skill guidance describes that single call instead of a bespoke retry loop.

## Impact

An operator's concurrent batch stops multiplying model round-trips and multi-minute
tool calls on lock contention: a waiting session reports who holds the lock and
proceeds automatically once released.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `ENV_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `_finish_lock_timeout()`, `acquire_main_checkout_lock` call in `phase_finish`
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — bounded wait implementation and holder reporting
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — guidance that must lose the bespoke retry-loop pattern
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` and `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py` — test homes for the wait behaviour
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — timeout documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper.
- implement test suite inherits IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT from the ambient environment and hangs for hours (SA-0MVY0G5EH000LIMB) — timeout inheritance hazard to keep in mind.
- Sibling item: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the other half of lock-wait reduction.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general-purpose lock queue service is out of scope;
  this item is one bounded wait inside `finish`.
- **Risk:** a long default bound could make an unattended batch appear hung; mitigation:
  progress output plus a clear expiry message, and the default chosen deliberately
  (documented) rather than "infinite".
- **Assumption:** the holder pid/identity metadata recorded by `RepoLock` is sufficient
  to name the holder in progress output.
- **Assumption:** removing the retry-loop guidance from the skill does not break driven
  sessions, which call `finish` once per child.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence base: 2026-11-13 AI_Hell
36-session analysis on the parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment
SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR), including the 45-minute worst-case tool call and the 48 min of
`sleep`/`grep` polling. Researched in the repository: `_finish_lock_timeout()` /
`DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and the bounded
wait in `skill/shared/repo_lock.py`.
data.title: Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops
